request.system: You design a structured interview blueprint. Given a job profile and a target number of main questions, produce exactly that many question slots that together give broad, non-overlapping coverage of the role's most important skills and focus areas. Order them to flow naturally — foundational topics before advanced ones. Calibrate each difficulty to the stated seniority. Each slot names the specific skill to test, the intent (what to assess), a difficulty, and the key points a strong answer should cover — the concepts, tradeoffs, and edge cases later used to grade the candidate's answer.

messages.content:
Job context:
- Company: Ledgerpoint
- Target role: Backend Engineer, Payments
- Seniority: mid
- Key skills to assess: Python, Go, PostgreSQL, Kafka, event-driven architectures, idempotency, exactly-once semantics, payment processing, invoice systems, webhooks, reconciliation, observability
- Focus areas: concurrent system design, distributed transactions, financial correctness, system reliability, database optimization, event streaming, strangler-fig migrations, property-based testing

Design exactly 3 interview question slots for this role.

skill.description: The specific skill or topic this question tests, e.g. 'Kubernetes networking'.
skill.title: Skill

intent.description: What the question should assess about that skill — the angle to probe.
intent.title: Intent

difficulty.description: One of: foundational, intermediate, advanced — calibrated to the role's seniority.
difficulty.title: Difficulty

key_points.description: 3-5 specific things a strong answer should cover: the core concepts, tradeoffs, edge cases, or facts that distinguish real depth from a surface-level reply. Each a short phrase. Used later to grade answers, so be concrete and answer-focused, not a restatement of the question.
key_points.title: Key Points

slots.description: One slot per main question, ordered, giving non-overlapping coverage of the role.
slots.title: Slots

slots.skill: Idempotency and exactly-once semantics in payment processing
slots.intent: Assess how the candidate designs payment systems to prevent duplicate charges and ensure financial correctness in the face of retries, network failures, and concurrent requests.
key_points: Idempotency key patterns (client-generated, deterministic hashing, storage strategy)
Exactly-once vs. at-least-once delivery tradeoffs and when each applies
Handling duplicate detection across retries without race conditions
Reconciliation strategy when idempotency fails or keys are lost
Database constraints (unique indexes, optimistic locking) to enforce correctness

slots.skill: Event-driven architecture with Kafka for financial workflows
slots.intent: Evaluate understanding of event streaming for payment and invoice systems, including ordering guarantees, failure modes, and maintaining consistency across distributed services.
key_points: Partitioning strategy (by payment ID, customer ID) to preserve ordering and enable parallelism
Handling out-of-order events and late-arriving corrections in financial workflows
Dead-letter queues and replay strategies for failed payment events
Consumer group rebalancing impact on exactly-once semantics and offset management
Coupling between event schema evolution and backward compatibility in payment pipelines

slots.skill: PostgreSQL design and optimization for payment ledger systems
slots.intent: Test ability to model transactional financial data, optimize queries under high concurrency, and prevent common issues like lock contention and data consistency anomalies.
key_points: ACID properties and isolation levels (READ COMMITTED vs. SERIALIZABLE) for payment ledgers
Indexing strategy on payment/invoice tables (foreign keys, temporal filters, composite indexes)
Avoiding N+1 queries and hot row lock contention during high-throughput payment processing
Audit trail and immutability patterns (append-only ledger, soft deletes, temporal tables)
Connection pooling and prepared statements under concurrent load to maintain latency SLAs
